So maybe the Tomcats are struggling because they can't keep up with the data being processed, leading to frequent garbage collection.

So if there's an issue in the upstream components, it affects the downstream services.

Maybe the underlying databases (Mysql or Redis) are not responding quickly enough, causing the Tomcats to hold onto more data, leading to memory pressure.

Another angle is the disk activity. MG01's sdb disk has very high read/write rates, possibly due to heavy database queries. If the disks are under stress, that could affect the performance of Mysql and Redis, which rely on disk I/O. High disk usage might lead to slower response times, which in turn makes the applications (like Tomcat) work harder, leading to increased CPU and memory use.

Also, the NTP offset for Mysql02 is slightly off, but that might not be the main issue. The critical part seems to be the disk I/O and memory pressure. Since the Tomcats are dependent on both Mysql and Redis, any delay in those systems would impact the Tomcats, leading to GC issues.

So putting it all together, the root causes might be related to the disk I/O problems in MG01, which affects Mysql and Redis, leading to increased load on Tomcat, causing GC issues. Alternatively, the high memory usage in Redis02 could be contributing to the overall system strain. But considering the propagation path and the fact that MG01 is upstream to Tomcat, which in turn depends on MG, Mysql, and Redis, the primary culprit is probably the disk issues in MG01. Then, the subsequent effects on Mysql and Redis, and finally the GC in Tomcat. Therefore, the top three components would be MG01 (due to disk I/O), Redis02 (memory pressure), and Tomcat01-04 (as the downstream affected services).
